summary: A husband who sent a get may cancel it before it reaches his wife. Once she has it in her hand, he can no longer cancel it.

chunks.en: Someone who sends a get to his wife, and he caught up with the messenger,
chunks.st: In the case of one who sends a bill of divorce to his wife with an agent, and he reached the agent,

chunks.he: אוֹ שֶׁשָּׁלַח אַחֲרָיו שָׁלִיחַ וְאָמַר לוֹ,
chunks.en: or he sent another messenger after him and said to him,
chunks.st: or where he sent another agent after him, and he said to the agent delivering the bill of divorce:

chunks.en: "The get that I gave you is cancelled,"
chunks.st: The bill of divorce that I gave you, it is void,

chunks.en: then it is cancelled.
chunks.st: then this bill of divorce is hereby void.

chunks.en: If he got to his wife first, or he sent
chunks.st: Similarly, if the husband reached his wife before the bill of divorce reached her, or in a case where he sent

chunks.en: a messenger to her and said to her,
chunks.st: an agent to her, and he said, or had the agent say, to his wife:

chunks.en: "The get that I sent you is cancelled,"
chunks.st: The bill of divorce that I sent to you, it is void,

chunks.en: then it is cancelled.
chunks.st: then this bill of divorce is hereby void.

chunks.en: But once the get has reached her hand,
chunks.st: However, if he stated this once the bill of divorce had entered her possession,

chunks.en: he can no longer cancel it.
chunks.st: he can no longer render it void, as the divorce had already taken effect.

summary: Rabban Gamliel the Elder made two rules to help the world: a husband may not cancel a get secretly in another beis din, and a get must include all the names the husband and wife are known by.

chunks.en: At first, a husband would make a beis
chunks.st: The mishna relates that initially, a husband who wished to render the bill of divorce void would convene a court

chunks.en: din in another place and cancel the get there.
chunks.st: elsewhere and render the bill of divorce void in the presence of the court before it reached his wife.

chunks.en: Rabban Gamliel the Elder made a rule
chunks.st: Rabban Gamliel the Elder instituted an ordinance

chunks.en: that they should not do this,
chunks.st: that one should not do this,

chunks.en: to make the world better.
chunks.st: for the betterment of the world.
chunks.stMore: The Gemara will explain what this means.

chunks.en: At first, he would change his name and her name,
chunks.st: Initially, the husband would change his name and her name,
chunks.stMore: from the names by which they were known where they formerly lived to the names by which they were known where the bill of divorce was written, and write

chunks.en: and the name of his city and the name of her city.
chunks.st: the name of his city and the name of her city.
chunks.stMore: One was not required to list all of the names by which the husband and the wife were known, but only the names in the place where the bill of divorce was being written.

chunks.he: וְהִתְקִין רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הַזָּקֵן שֶׁיְּהֵא כוֹתֵב,
chunks.en: Rabban Gamliel the Elder made a rule that the scribe should write,
chunks.st: Rabban Gamliel the Elder instituted that the scribe should write in the bill of divorce:

chunks.he: אִישׁ פְּלוֹנִי וְכָל שֵׁם שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ,
chunks.en: "The man so-and-so, and every name he has,"
chunks.st: The man so-and-so, and any other name that he has,

chunks.he: אִשָּׁה פְלוֹנִית וְכָל שׁוּם שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהּ,
chunks.en: "The woman so-and-so, and every name she has,"
chunks.st: and: The woman so-and-so, and any other name that she has.

chunks.en: to make the world better.
chunks.st: The reason for this ordinance was for the betterment of the world,
chunks.stMore: as perhaps the people of a different city would not recognize the name written in the bill of divorce, and would claim that this bill of divorce does not belong to her.

summary: A widow must swear before collecting her kesubah from orphans. Rabban Gamliel let her make a promise instead. The mishnah lists more rules made to help the world, like Hillel's pruzbul.

chunks.en: A widow may not collect from the property
chunks.st: A widow can collect payment of her marriage contract from the property of orphans

chunks.en: of orphans unless she swears.
chunks.st: only by means of an oath
chunks.stMore: that she did not receive any part of the payment of the marriage contract during her husband’s lifetime. The mishna relates:

chunks.en: The courts stopped making her swear,
chunks.st: The courts refrained from administering an oath to her,
chunks.stMore: leaving the widow unable to collect payment of her marriage contract.

chunks.en: so Rabban Gamliel the Elder made a rule that she should
chunks.st: Rabban Gamliel the Elder instituted that she should take, for

chunks.en: make any promise to the orphans that they want,
chunks.st: the benefit of the orphans, any vow that the orphans wished to administer to her,
chunks.stMore: e.g., that all produce will become prohibited to her if she received any payment of her marriage contract,

chunks.en: and then she collects her kesubah.
chunks.st: and after stating this vow, she collects payment of her marriage contract.
chunks.stMore: The mishna lists additional ordinances that were instituted for the betterment of the world:

words.note: The kesubah promises money to a wife if the marriage ends.

chunks.en: The witnesses sign on the get,
chunks.st: The witnesses sign their names on the bill of divorce,
chunks.stMore: even though the bill of divorce is valid without their signatures,

chunks.en: to make the world better.
chunks.st: for the betterment of the world,
chunks.stMore: as the Gemara will explain.

chunks.he: הִלֵּל הִתְקִין פְּרוֹזְבּוּל מִפְּנֵּי תִקּוּן הָעוֹלָם:
chunks.en: Hillel made the pruzbul to make the world better.
chunks.explain: A pruzbul lets a lender collect his loan even after Shemitah.
chunks.st: And Hillel instituted a document that prevents the Sabbatical Year from abrogating an outstanding debt [prosbol] for the betterment of the world, as the Gemara will explain.

summary: This mishnah teaches what happens to a slave who was redeemed from captors, and to a slave who was promised to pay a debt and then set free.

chunks.en: A slave who was captured, and someone redeemed him,
chunks.st: In the case of a Canaanite slave that was captured, and Jews who had not owned him redeemed him,

chunks.en: if it was to be a slave,
chunks.st: if he was redeemed to be a slave

chunks.en: he stays a slave. If it was to be free,
chunks.st: then he will be a slave. If he was redeemed to be a freeman

chunks.en: he does not stay a slave.
chunks.st: then he will not be a slave.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says,
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

chunks.en: either way, he stays a slave.
chunks.st: Both in this case and in that case he will be a slave.

chunks.he: עֶבֶד שֶׁעֲשָׂאוֹ רַבּוֹ אַפּוֹתִיקִי לַאֲחֵרִים וְשִׁחְרְרוֹ,
chunks.en: A slave whose master promised him to others to pay a debt, and then set him free:
chunks.st: In the case of a slave whose master set him aside as designated repayment [apoteiki] of a debt to other people from whom he borrowed money, and afterward he emancipated him,

chunks.en: by the strict law,
chunks.st: then according to the letter of the law

chunks.en: the slave does not owe anything.
chunks.st: the slave bears no responsibility for the debt.

chunks.en: But to make the world better,
chunks.st: However, for the betterment of the world,

chunks.en: we force his master to make
chunks.st: his master is forced to make

chunks.en: him a free man,
chunks.st: him a freeman, and

chunks.en: and the slave writes a note promising to pay his value.
chunks.st: the slave writes a promissory note for his value to pay the debt to the creditor.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says,
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

chunks.en: the slave does not write anything, but the master just frees him.
chunks.st: He does not write a promissory note; he only emancipates the slave.

summary: A slave who is half free cannot marry anyone. Beis Shammai taught that his master must free him, and Beis Hillel agreed with them in the end.

chunks.he: מִי שֶׁחֶצְיוֹ עֶבֶד וְחֶצְיוֹ בֶן חוֹרִין,
chunks.en: Someone who is half a slave and half free,
chunks.st: In the case of one who is a half-slave half-freeman because only one of his two owners emancipated him,

chunks.en: works for his master one day
chunks.st: he serves his master one day and

chunks.en: and for himself one day.
chunks.st: serves himself one day;

chunks.en: These are the words of Beis Hillel.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Beit Hillel.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai said to them,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

chunks.en: "You fixed things for his master,
chunks.st: Through such an arrangement you have remedied his master,
chunks.stMore: as his master loses nothing through this. However,

chunks.en: but you did not fix things for himself.
chunks.st: you have not remedied the slave himself,
chunks.stMore: as the slave himself remains in an unsustainable situation.

chunks.en: He cannot marry a maidservant,
chunks.st: It is not possible for him to marry a maidservant

chunks.en: since he is already half free.
chunks.st: because he is already a half-freeman,
chunks.stMore: as it is prohibited for a freeman to marry a maidservant.

chunks.en: He cannot marry a free woman,
chunks.st: It is also not possible for him to marry a free woman,

chunks.en: since he is still half a slave.
chunks.st: as he is still a half-slave.

chunks.en: Should he not marry at all? But the world was created
chunks.st: If you say he should be idle and not marry, but isn’t it true that the world was created

chunks.en: only for having children,
chunks.st: only for procreation,

chunks.en: as it says: He did not create it to be empty,
chunks.st: as it is stated: “He did not create it to be a waste;

chunks.en: He formed it to be lived in.
chunks.st: He formed it to be inhabited” (Isaiah 45:18)?

chunks.en: Rather, to make the world better,
chunks.st: Rather, for the betterment of the world

chunks.en: we force his master to make
chunks.st: his master is forced to make

chunks.en: him a free man,
chunks.st: him a freeman, and

chunks.en: and the slave writes a note promising to pay half his value."
chunks.st: the slave writes a promissory note accepting his responsibility to pay half his value to his master.

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel changed their minds to teach
chunks.st: And Beit Hillel ultimately retracted their opinion,

chunks.en: like the words of Beis Shammai.
chunks.st: to rule in accordance with the statement of Beit Shammai, that a half-slave must be set free.

summary: A slave sold to a non-Jew goes free. To help the world, we do not pay too much to free captives, help them escape, or buy back holy things for too much money.

chunks.he: הַמּוֹכֵר עַבְדּוֹ לְגוֹי אוֹ לְחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ,
chunks.en: Someone who sells his slave to a non-Jew or to someone outside Eretz Yisrael,
chunks.st: In a case of one who sells his slave to gen-tiles, or even to a Jew outside of Eretz Yisrael,

chunks.en: the slave goes out free.
chunks.st: the slave is emancipated.
chunks.stMore: Since the slave, who is partially obligated in the fulfillment of mitzvot, would be restricted in his ability to fulfill them in his new situation, either because he would be under the authority of a gentile or because he will no longer be in Eretz Yisrael, the Sages penalized his original owner that he should become a freeman, so that if he succeeds in escaping his new owner, he is a full-fledged freeman.

chunks.en: We do not redeem captives
chunks.st: The captives are not redeemed

chunks.en: for more than they are worth,
chunks.st: for more than their actual monetary value,

chunks.en: to make the world better.
chunks.st: for the betterment of the world;

chunks.en: And we do not help captives run away,
chunks.st: and one may not aid the captives in their attempt to escape from their captors

chunks.en: to make the world better.
chunks.st: for the betterment of the world,
chunks.stMore: so that kidnappers will not be more restrictive with their captives to prevent them from escaping.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says,
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

chunks.en: it is to help the other captives.
chunks.explain: So the captors will not be cruel to the ones left behind.
chunks.st: For the betterment of the captives,
chunks.stMore: so that kidnappers will not avenge the escape of the captives by treating other captives with cruelty.

chunks.en: And we do not buy sifrei Torah,
chunks.st: And Torah scrolls,

chunks.en: tefillin, and mezuzos from non-Jews
chunks.st: phylacteries, or mezuzot are not purchased from the gentiles
chunks.stMore: when they acquire these objects, if they request

chunks.en: for more than they are worth,
chunks.st: more than their actual monetary value,

chunks.en: to make the world better.
chunks.st: for the betterment of the world, so as not to cause an increase in the theft of sacred Jewish ritual objects in order to sell them for large sums of money.

summary: If a man divorced his wife because of a bad name or because of a neder, he may not marry her again. The Rabbis argue about which nedarim this applies to.

chunks.he: הַמּוֹצִיא אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ מִשּׁוּם שֵׁם רָע,
chunks.en: Someone who sends away his wife because of a bad name,
chunks.st: A man who divorces his wife due to her bad reputation,

chunks.en: may not take her back.
chunks.st: i.e., he heard that she had committed adultery, may not remarry her,
chunks.stMore: even if it becomes clear that she did not in fact commit adultery.

chunks.en: Because of a neder,
chunks.st: Similarly, if one divorces his wife due to a vow
chunks.stMore: that she took, and he could not live with her under the conditions of her vow,

words.note: A neder is a promise that makes something forbidden.

chunks.en: he may not take her back.
chunks.st: he may not remarry her.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: any neder that many people knew about,
chunks.st: If he divorces her due to any vow that the public was aware of,

chunks.en: he may not take her back.
chunks.st: he may not remarry her,

chunks.en: But one that many people did not know about,
chunks.st: but if he divorces her due to a vow that the public was not aware of,

chunks.en: he may take her back. Rabbi Meir says,
chunks.st: he may remarry her. The mishna continues: Rabbi Meir says:

chunks.en: any neder that needs a Sage to look into it,
chunks.st: If he divorces her due to any vow that requires investigation and dissolution by a halakhic authority,

chunks.en: he may not take her back.
chunks.st: he may not bring remarry her,

chunks.en: But one that does not need a Sage to look into it,
chunks.st: but if he divorces her due to a vow that does not require investigation and dissolution by a halakhic authority, and is dissolved even without that,

chunks.en: he may take her back. Rabbi Eliezer said,
chunks.st: he may bring remarry her. Rabbi Elazar said:

chunks.he: לֹא אָסְרוּ זֶה אֶלָּא מִפְּנֵי זֶה.
chunks.en: they forbade this one only because of that one.
chunks.st: They prohibited him from remarrying her in this case, where she stated a vow that requires dissolution by a halakhic authority, only due to that
chunks.stMore: case, where she stated a vow that does not require dissolution by a halakhic authority.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei the son of Rabbi Yehuda said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, said:

chunks.en: once in Tzaidan, a man said to his wife,
chunks.st: There was an incident in Tzaidan involving one man who said to his wife:

chunks.en: "Konam, if I do not divorce you!"
chunks.explain: Konam is a word for a neder.
chunks.st: It is konam, i.e., it is forbidden like an offering, if I do not divorce you,

chunks.en: and he divorced her. And the Sages let him take her back,
chunks.st: and he divorced her; and the Sages permitted him to remarry her

chunks.en: to make the world better.
chunks.st: for the betterment of the world.

summary: If a man divorced his wife because he thought she could never have children, may he marry her again? And what if she later had children with someone else?

chunks.en: Someone who sends away his wife because she cannot have children,
chunks.st: With regard to one who divorces his wife because she is a sexually underdeveloped woman who is incapable of bearing children [ailonit],
chunks.stMore: meaning that after their marriage it became clear that she was sexually underdeveloped,

words.note: A woman who cannot have children.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: he may not take her back.
chunks.st: He may not remarry her,

chunks.en: And the Sages say,
chunks.st: and the Rabbis say:

chunks.he: יַחֲזִיר. נִשֵּׂאת לְאַחֵר וְהָיוּ לָהּ בָּנִים הֵימֶנּוּ,
chunks.en: he may take her back. If she married someone else and had children with him,
chunks.st: He may remarry her. If, after he divorced her, this ailonit married another man and had children from him,
chunks.stMore: meaning that she was not actually an ailonit,

chunks.en: and she asks for her kesubah money,
chunks.st: and she is demanding payment of her marriage contract from her first husband,
chunks.stMore: claiming that he unlawfully divorced her without paying her marriage contract as he claimed that she was an ailonit and their marriage was a mistaken transaction,

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda said that

chunks.en: he may say to her,
chunks.st: he may say to her:

chunks.en: "Your quiet is better for you than your speaking."
chunks.explain: It is better for her not to ask.
chunks.st: Your silence is preferable to your speech,
chunks.stMore: meaning that it is preferable for her to withdraw her claim. If she persists, he may say that he divorced her only because he believed her to be an ailonit, casting aspersions on the validity of the divorce and the status of her children. Therefore, it would be wise of her to withdraw her claim.

summary: A man who sold himself and his children to a non-Jew is not redeemed, but his children are. A field sold to a non-Jew still needs bikkurim when a Jew buys it back.

chunks.he: הַמּוֹכֵר אֶת עַצְמוֹ וְאֶת בָּנָיו לְגוֹי,
chunks.en: Someone who sells himself and his children to a non-Jew,
chunks.st: With regard to one who sells himself and his children as slaves to gentiles,

chunks.en: we do not redeem him,
chunks.st: he is not redeemed,

chunks.en: but we do redeem the children
chunks.st: but the children are redeemed

chunks.en: after their father dies.
chunks.st: after their father’s death,
chunks.stMore: as there is no reason to penalize them.

chunks.en: Someone who sells his field to a non-Jew, and then
chunks.st: One who sells his field to a gentile

chunks.en: a Jew bought it back from him,
chunks.st: must purchase
chunks.basisNote: Steinsaltz reads it as the seller buying it back; these words follow our Hebrew text.

chunks.en: the buyer brings bikkurim from it,
chunks.st: and bring the first fruits from the field that he sold,

words.note: The first fruits, brought to the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: to make the world better.
chunks.st: for the betterment of the world.
